title: What education and training do Japan's GQP and GVP ordinances require of marketing authorization holders?
seoTitle: Japan GQP and GVP training requirements
description: Training duties for Japanese marketing authorization holders under the GQP Ordinance (No. 136) and GVP Ordinance (No. 135): plans, records and retention.
shortAnswer: Japan's GQP Ordinance (MHLW Ordinance No. 136 of 2004) and GVP Ordinance (No. 135 of 2004) require marketing authorization holders to train staff in quality control and post-marketing safety work. Each needs a written training procedure, a training plan, planned delivery by a designated person, training records kept five years, and written reporting to the quality assurance or safety management responsible person. GVP training applies to Type 1 and Type 2 license holders only.
keyTakeaways: Article 14 of the GQP Ordinance requires a drug marketing authorization holder (MAH) to have a designated person prepare a training plan for quality control staff, deliver training systematically, record it, and report in writing to the quality assurance responsible person when someone else runs it.

Article 12 of the GVP Ordinance requires the general marketing compliance officer to prepare and keep the training plan, a designated person to deliver planned post-marketing safety training, and the safety management responsible person to report results in writing to the general marketing compliance officer.
Both ordinances fix training record retention at five years from creation, overriding the longer periods that apply to other records for biological and regenerative products.

GVP training applies to Type 1 MAHs (prescription drugs, highly controlled devices, regenerative products) and Type 2 MAHs (non-prescription drugs, controlled devices, in vitro diagnostics), but not Type 3 (quasi-drugs, cosmetics, general devices).
From May 20, 2027, MHLW Ordinance No. 142 of 2026 renames the responsible persons and extends the GQP quality assurance unit and training article to quasi-drug MAHs; GVP Article 12 is unchanged.
regulator: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW), with prefectural governments handling most marketing license administration and inspection
appliesTo: Marketing authorization holders (seizō hanbaigyōsha) for drugs and regenerative medicine products, for GQP Article 14
Type 1 and Type 2 marketing authorization holders for drugs, medical devices, in vitro diagnostics and regenerative products, for GVP Article 12
General marketing compliance officers, quality assurance responsible persons and safety management responsible persons
Quality control, storage and post-marketing safety staff, including medical representatives who collect safety information

sections.heading: Where do the GQP and GVP training duties come from?

blocks.text: Both ordinances are conditions of the marketing license (seizō hanbaigyō kyoka) under the Act on Securing Quality, Efficacy and Safety of Products Including Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices (the PMD Act, 医薬品医療機器等法, Act No. 145 of 1960). Article 12-2 of the Act allows the license to be refused where the applicant's quality control method fails the standard set by ministerial ordinance (item 1) or its post-marketing safety management method fails the standard (item 2) ([PMD Act, e-Gov](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/335AC0000000145)).

Those standards are the **Ministerial Ordinance on Good Quality Practice** (医薬品、医薬部外品、化粧品及び再生医療等製品の品質管理の基準に関する省令, MHLW Ordinance No. 136 of 2004, GQP) and the **Ministerial Ordinance on Good Vigilance Practice** (医薬品、医薬部外品、化粧品、医療機器及び再生医療等製品の製造販売後安全管理の基準に関する省令, MHLW Ordinance No. 135 of 2004, GVP). GQP governs the MAH's quality control work: release to market, oversight of manufacturers, quality complaints and recalls. GVP governs collection, assessment and action on safety information after marketing. Manufacturing sites follow the separate GMP ordinance; see [Japan's GMP personnel training requirements](/regulations/japan-gmp-personnel-training-requirements).

Japan separates the marketing license from manufacturing licenses, so an MAH may not manufacture anything itself. Its training duties therefore center on oversight roles: the general marketing compliance officer (sōkatsu seizō hanbai sekininsha), who must be a pharmacist for drug MAHs under Article 17 of the Act; the quality assurance responsible person (hinshitsu hoshō sekininsha); and the safety management responsible person (anzen kanri sekininsha).

Article 14 of the GQP Ordinance has two paragraphs. Paragraph 1 requires the drug MAH to have a person designated in advance prepare an education and training plan for the people engaged in quality control work. Paragraph 2 requires the MAH, under its quality control procedures and that plan, to have the designated person:

items: systematically deliver education and training on quality control work to the people engaged in it, and create records of it; and
where someone other than the quality assurance responsible person does this work, report the status of training in writing to the quality assurance responsible person.

blocks.text: Source: [GQP Ordinance, e-Gov](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/416M60000100136). Article 6(1)(vi) requires a written procedure for education and training among the ten mandatory quality control procedures. Article 4(4) requires the duties and management structure of everyone engaged in quality control, including the general marketing compliance officer and the quality assurance responsible person, to be set out in writing, which defines the training population.

Competence also appears outside Article 14. Article 4(1) requires sufficient personnel able to carry out quality control work properly. Article 4(3) requires the quality assurance responsible person to head the quality assurance unit, to have at least three years in quality control or similar work, and not to belong to a sales department. Article 15(2) requires staff who store or display drugs for marketing to have the necessary capability and to have received the necessary education and training.
Article 12 of the GVP Ordinance gives the training plan a more senior owner. It requires a Type 1 MAH to:

items: have the general marketing compliance officer prepare and keep an education and training plan;
under the post-marketing safety procedures and that plan, have a designated person deliver planned education and training on post-marketing safety management to the people engaged in it;
where the designated person is the safety management responsible person, have that person create and keep the training records;

where the designated person is someone else, have that person create the records, report in writing to the safety management responsible person, and have the records kept by the safety management responsible person; and
have the safety management responsible person report the results of training in writing to the general marketing compliance officer and keep a copy.

blocks.text: Source: [GVP Ordinance, e-Gov](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/416M60000100135). Article 5(1)(ix) lists a procedure for training post-marketing safety staff among the mandatory GVP procedures, and Article 4 requires a safety management unit independent of sales, headed by a safety management responsible person with at least three years in safety assurance or similar work.

The training population is wide. GVP Article 2 defines medical representatives (iyaku jōhō tantōsha), medical device information representatives and regenerative product information representatives as staff whose main work is visiting health professionals to collect and provide safety information. Where they collect safety information under the MAH's procedures, they are engaged in post-marketing safety work and belong in the training plan.

sections.heading: Which license holders are covered by each training article?

blocks.text: Coverage depends on the product and, for GVP, the license class. GQP Chapter 2, including Article 14, applies to drug MAHs and, through Article 21, to regenerative medicine product MAHs. Quasi-drug and cosmetic MAHs follow the lighter Chapter 3, which as at November 2026 has no training article, except for quasi-drugs the Minister designates as needing care in quality control, which follow Chapter 2. GVP classes are defined in Article 2.

sections.heading: How long must GQP and GVP training records be kept?

blocks.text: Five years from creation under both ordinances. GQP Article 16(3)(d) sets five years for education and training documents and records "regardless of" the periods for other records, which run to the expiry date plus 30 years for specified biological products, plus 10 years for other biological and cell or tissue products, and the longer of five years or expiry plus one year for other drugs. GVP Article 16(1)(iv) likewise sets five years from creation for self-inspection and training records, while other GVP records run five years from last use, or 10, 15 or 30 years for biological, specially maintained device and specified biological products.

The practical consequence is that training records can usually be archived on a shorter cycle than batch or safety records. Training plans themselves are documents, so under GVP they follow the general five-years-from-last-use rule. See [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records) for a cross-jurisdiction view.

sections.heading: Do the 2025 PMD Act amendments change these training duties?

blocks.text: Not in substance yet, but quasi-drug MAHs should prepare. Comparing versions on e-Gov, MHLW Ordinance No. 117 of 2025 changed only the definitions article of GVP from May 1, 2026, and left Article 12 untouched. MHLW Ordinance No. 142 of 2026, promulgated September 30, 2026, amends both ordinances from **May 20, 2027**, when the corresponding stage of the 2025 PMD Act amendment takes effect.

items: In GQP, the quality assurance responsible person becomes the drug quality assurance responsible person (iyakuhin hinshitsu hoshō sekininsha) defined in the amended Act, and Article 14's reporting line is renamed accordingly.
A new GQP structure for quasi-drug MAHs (Articles 20-2 to 20-5) requires a quality assurance unit and, through Article 20-5, applies Article 14 training to quasi-drug MAHs.
In GVP, Article 4 is restructured around the drug safety management responsible person defined in Article 17(6) of the amended Act, while the text of Article 12 is unchanged.

blocks.text: As at November 2026, these changes are promulgated but not in force. Quasi-drug MAHs that have never needed a GQP training plan will need one, with records, from May 20, 2027.

blocks.text: Because neither ordinance sets a refresher interval, the plan should state one and justify it, typically by role, by procedure revision and by self-inspection findings, which both ordinances require to be performed periodically.

sections.heading: What happens if GQP or GVP training is inadequate?

blocks.text: Training gaps are GQP or GVP nonconformities, and the PMD Act treats nonconformity with either standard as a license matter. Article 72(1) lets the Minister order an MAH whose quality control or post-marketing safety method fails the ordinance standard to improve it, or to suspend all or part of its business until it does. Article 75(1) allows license revocation or business suspension for violations of the Act and related orders. Missing training records also undermine the self-inspection and management review evidence that inspectors use to judge whether the system works.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models GQP Articles 6, 14, 15 and 16 and GVP Articles 5, 12 and 16 as obligations linked to the MAH's own procedures and named roles, then defines learning outcomes and assessment points before training is written. The May 2027 renaming and quasi-drug extension can be entered as dated changes against the same obligations.

faqs.q: Do the GQP or GVP ordinances set a minimum training frequency?
faqs.a: No. Both require training to be delivered systematically under a written plan and procedure, but neither sets an interval. The MAH should define frequency in its training plan, usually at assignment, on procedure revision and periodically thereafter, and justify it through self-inspection results.

faqs.q: Who signs off the GVP training plan?
faqs.a: Under GVP Article 12(1), the general marketing compliance officer prepares and keeps the plan. Delivery can be delegated to a designated person, but the safety management responsible person must report the results in writing to the general marketing compliance officer and keep a copy.

faqs.q: Do cosmetic companies in Japan need a GQP training plan?
faqs.a: Not as at November 2026. Cosmetic and most quasi-drug MAHs follow GQP Chapter 3, which has no training article, and Type 3 MAHs are outside GVP Article 12. From May 20, 2027, quasi-drug MAHs gain a quality assurance unit and the Article 14 training duty under MHLW Ordinance No. 142 of 2026.

faqs.q: Are medical representatives covered by GVP training?
faqs.a: They are when they collect or provide safety information as part of post-marketing safety work. GVP Article 2 defines medical representatives by that information role, and Article 12 covers everyone engaged in post-marketing safety management, so MAHs normally include them in the GVP training plan.
